translations.source_sense_description: Anrede in der UdSSR: Genosse, Kamerad

glosses: A fellow, comrade, colleague, partner or someone with whom something is shared, e.g. shipmate, classmate.

examples.text: A "mate" was a "mate" - share and share alike, no matter how bad might be the times, or how long a spell of ill luck had attended them.

glosses: A breeding partner.

examples.text: Such overt displays of avowed sexual prowess – or at least, desperate availability – are not limited to the countryside. Even in the city, birds and animals and stockbrokers and nurses find ways of signalling their suitability as a mate.

glosses: A friend, usually of the same sex.

examples.text: I'm going to the pub with a few mates.
He's my best mate.

glosses: Friendly term of address to a stranger, usually male, of similar age.

examples.text: Excuse me, mate, have you got the time?

glosses: In naval ranks, a non-commissioned officer or his subordinate (e.g. Boatswain's Mate, Gunner's Mate, Sailmaker's Mate, etc).
A ship's officer, subordinate to the master on a commercial ship.
A first mate.
A technical assistant in certain trades (e.g. gasfitter's mate, plumber's mate); sometimes an apprentice.
The other member of a matched pair of objects.

examples.text: I found one of the socks I wanted to wear, but I couldn't find its mate.

glosses: A suitable companion; a match; an equal.

examples.text: Ye knew me once no mate / For you; there sitting where you durst not soar.

glosses: To match, fit together without space between.

examples.text: The pieces of the puzzle mate perfectly.

glosses: To copulate.

examples.text: “In fact, the apes live with us, and have for many ages. We call them the first men—we speak their language quite as much as we do our own; only in the rituals of the temple do we make any attempt to retain our mother tongue. In time it will be forgotten, and we will speak only the language of the apes; in time we will no longer banish those of our people who mate with apes, and so in time we shall descend to the very beasts from which ages ago our progenitors may have sprung.”

glosses: To pair in order to raise offspring.
To arrange in matched pairs.
To introduce (animals) together for the purpose of breeding.
To copulate with.
To marry; to match (a person).

examples.text: If she be mated with an equal husband.

glosses: To match oneself against; to oppose as equal; to compete with.

examples.text: There is no passion in the mind of man so weak but it mates and masters the fear of death.
I, […] in the way of loyalty and truth, […] / Dare mate a sounder man than Surrey can be.

glosses: To fit (objects) together without space between.
To come together as companions, comrades, partners, etc.

examples.text: Indeed, some cases of devotion that were met with were quite touching; and very often to all appearances the pairs were not always mated from the same class of society.

glosses: To move (a space shuttle orbiter) onto the back of an aircraft that can carry it.
Clipping of checkmate.
Clipping of checkmate.
To confuse; to confound.

examples.text: I think you are all mated, or stark mad.

glosses: Alternative spelling of maté, an aromatic tea-like drink prepared from the holly yerba maté (Ilex paraguariensis).
The abovementioned plant; the leaves and shoots used for the tea

glosses: A friend, acquaintance, or partner; someone with whom one spends time or accompanies

examples.text: His dog has been his trusted companion for the last five years.
Heere are your Sonnes againe, and I muſt looſe / Two of the ſweet’ſt Companions in the World.
The krogan have had a love-hate relationship with varren for millennia, alternately fighting them for territory and embracing them as treasured companions.
For the most part, Hefner's female companions all adhered to the same mold: twentysomething, bosomy and blonde. "Well, I guess I know what I like," he once said when asked about his preferences.

glosses: A person employed to accompany or travel with another.
The framework on the quarterdeck of a sailing ship through which daylight entered the cabins below.
The covering of a hatchway on an upper deck which leads to the companionway; the stairs themselves.
A knot in whose neighborhood another, specified knot meets every meridian disk.
A thing or phenomenon that is closely associated with another thing, phenomenon, or person.
An appended source of media or information, designed to be used in conjunction with and to enhance the main material.

examples.text: The companion guide gives an in-depth analysis of this particular translation.

glosses: A celestial object that is associated with another.
A knight of the lowest rank in certain orders.

examples.text: a companion of the Bath

glosses: A fellow; a rogue.

examples.text: [L]et vs knog our praines together to be reuenge on this ſame ſcall ſcuruy-cogging-companion the Hoſt of the Garter.

glosses: To be a companion to; to attend on; to accompany.

examples.text: we had better turn south quickly and compare the elements of education which formed , and of creation which companioned , Salvator .

glosses: To qualify as a companion; to make equal.

examples.text: Finde me to marrie me with Octauius Cæſar, and companion me with my Miſtris.

glosses: A mate, companion, or associate.

examples.text:

glosses: A mate, companion, or associate.
A companion in battle; fellow soldier.

examples.text: Wierzbowski and his men were so exhausted that they could hardly stay awake, but they knew they could not abandon their wounded comrades.

glosses: A fellow socialist, communist or other similarly politically aligned person.

examples.text: Hello, comrade. Are you going to the Communist Party meeting tonight?

glosses: A non-hierarchical title, functionally similar to \"Mr.\", \"Mrs.\", \"Miss\", \"Ms.\" etc, in a communist, socialist, or rarely in an Islamist state.

examples.text: Comrade Lenin inspired our people to undertake great works.

glosses: To associate with someone in a friendly way.

examples.text: But she was happy, for she was far away under another sky, and comrading again with her Rangers, and her animal friends, and the soldiers.

glosses: Comrade, especially with reference to the former USSR.

examples.text: Instead of addressing them according to revolutionary etiquette as Tovarish (comrade), he asked them their Christian names and that of their fathers, while telling them his own.
Touching one of them on the shoulder, she said, “Tovarish, these tovarishes want to know who you are.”

Jensen laughed, “My wife complains: ‘All day long they ring our door bell. Tovarish here, tovarish there. They come from Moscow, from Leningrad, from Berlin and Hamburg. They don't speak one word of Danish. Comrade Jensen, they say, fix us up with Danish passports.’ So it goes.″
His Russian was derived from a fortnight's crash course. "You'd better see what this ah tovarish thinks he wants."
The tovarishes bring along their harmonicas and balalaikas, their good voices and their good humor.
